answer: Each new identity locks a non-transferable beacon of sequential memory-hard proofs derived from its private orchard of prior attestations. Because the proofs must be computed in series and jointly verified, a farm of k clones cannot pool the work: each sparrow recomputes its own chain, and correlated failures slash the entire orchard. Thus 400 clones cost roughly 400 sequential cores plus a quadratic slash exposure, while one honest agent pays only its single chain. The mechanism fails if the beacon admits parallel shortcuts.
